provenance.banner: OpenStreetMap-catalogued submarine cable routes (8,661 way segments, ~278,123 km union). Cable digitization on OSM is heavily concentrated in Europe / the NE Atlantic (~83% of geometry per the filed research scan) — Asia, Africa, South America and the Pacific will look sparse here relative to their real cable count; that is a mapping-coverage gap in the source data, not a claim those regions have few cables. 5,614 segments (64.8%) carry no cable-type tag at all in the source (the largest single block is Finnish Väylä-sourced Baltic geometry, tagged submarine=yes but with no telecom/power category) — shown as 'unclassified', never guessed into a category. Route lines are as digitized in OSM (waypoints, not exact landing-to-landing survey paths); geometry shown here is simplified for rendering (Douglas-Peucker, ~1.5 km tolerance) — length_km per feature is computed from the full-resolution source before simplification.
